# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 2 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_002_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 1, Chapter 2

**1** After saying these things to me she fell silent, and I saw her no more. I was overcome with trembling and grief and said to myself: "If even this is counted as sin against me, how can I be saved? How can I make amends to God for my many great and grave sins? By what words shall I ask the Lord for his mercy?" **2** While I was deliberating and debating these things in my heart, I saw before me a great white chair fashioned of the whitest wool. There came an aged woman dressed in gleaming clothing, holding a book in her hands. She sat down by herself and greeted me: "Greetings, Hermas." **3** I responded in grief and tears: "Greetings, my lady." She said to me, "Why are you so gloomy, Hermas — you, who are gentle and good-tempered and always cheerful? Why is your face downcast and not radiant?" **4** I said to her, "It is because of a fine woman who says I have sinned against her." She replied, "Far be that from a servant of God! Nevertheless, that thought concerning her did arise in your heart. A thought such as this is precisely what brings sin upon the servants of God. For it is an evil and ruinous disposition — when one who is upright desires an unworthy thing; and all the more so when Hermas, known for his self-control and avoidance of every evil desire, should entertain such a desire." **5** "However, it is not this alone for which God is displeased with you; it is also so that you might discipline your household, which has sinned against the Lord and against you, their parents. Although you love your children, you did not rebuke your household, but allowed it to sink into deep corruption. For this reason the Lord is displeased with you. Nevertheless he will restore all the former failures of your household; for through their sins and iniquities you have been worn down by the worries of this present age. **6** But the great mercy of the Lord has had compassion on you and your house, and will build you up and establish you in his glory. Only do not be slack, but take courage and build up your household. For just as a smith beats his craft into shape through repeated effort, so daily practice of righteousness will overcome all wickedness. Do not stop correcting your children; for I know that if they repent from their whole heart, they will be written in the books of life together with the saints."

---

*LOGOS note: "disposition" for intention-of-heart; "rebuke" preferred over "admonish" for stronger confrontational sense.*
